subject: Social Science
central_question: What are oceans and continents, how are they named and distributed across the Earth, and in what ways do they shape climate, life and human activity?
in_scope_units: Introduction: the Earth as the 'blue planet', water/land proportion, ocean/landmass/continent definitions
Distribution of Water and Land: uneven distribution between hemispheres, saltwater vs freshwater
Oceans: the five oceans, relative sizes, Indian Ocean boundaries, Arabian Sea/Bay of Bengal, marine flora/fauna
Oceans and disasters: monsoon, cyclones, tsunamis, 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, disaster management
Continents: why continents can be counted as four to seven, Olympic rings, relative sizes
Islands: definition, Greenland, India's island groups, Indian Antarctica Programme
Oceans and Life: water cycle, oxygen production, human uses, World Oceans Day, pollution/overfishing threats
banned_topics: Detailed treatment of latitude, longitude, map scale/directions/symbols and time zones (covered in Chapter 1)
Detailed description of mountains, plateaus, plains and other landforms (covered in Chapter 3)

known_pitfalls.claim: There is a fixed, universally agreed number of continents (always seven).
known_pitfalls.correction: Continents can be counted as four, five, six or seven depending on convention; seven is most widely adopted.

known_pitfalls.claim: The five oceans are completely separate bodies of water.
known_pitfalls.correction: The lines dividing oceans on maps are conventions - the natural world does not follow such boundaries.

known_pitfalls.claim: Most of Earth's abundant water is fit for humans and land animals to drink.
known_pitfalls.correction: Seawater is salty and unfit for consumption; freshwater is only a small proportion, in glaciers, rivers, lakes, atmosphere and underground.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Northern and Southern Hemispheres have an equal share of land and water.
known_pitfalls.correction: The Northern Hemisphere has more land than the Southern Hemisphere.

known_pitfalls.claim: Only islands are surrounded by water; continents are not.
known_pitfalls.correction: Continents are also surrounded by water, but are too large to be considered islands.

recommended_example_progression: Hemisphere-and-ocean identification exercise for the five oceans.
Continent-counting exercise comparing continent sizes and 'Eurasia'.
Reasoning exercise on defining Continent, Ocean, Island (NCERT Q1).
Disaster-awareness discussion on the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.
Revision exercise based on the end-of-chapter crossword on oceans and continents.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter's Questions, activities and projects section (numbered 1 to 4) covers defining continent/ocean/island, freehand drawing of continents, labelling a world map, and a crossword.
